transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. I came in because, well, I barely sleep right anymore. I'll just lie there at night, hearing the rain or... or just thinking about the bluff giving way. And then when I actually do pass out, I end up waking up all sweaty from these dreams. It's just getting really hard because I have to show up to my job at the call center every day feeling like I never even slept.
Did you go through a traumatic event involving the bluff giving way?
Yeah. I was out there when the bluff trail collapsed, and I got trapped. So... yeah, all this stuff with my sleep has been going on for about four months now, ever since that happened.
Do memories of the bluff collapse ever suddenly pop into your mind during the day, even when you don’t want them to?

Yeah, they do. Stuff just... pops in my head out of nowhere. Like, I'll suddenly hear the sound of the rocks sliding, or I'll remember the feeling of my leg being stuck under me. And just for a minute, it's like I'm right back out on that trail, instead of just sitting at my desk with my headset on.
Have you been avoiding anything that reminds you of the bluff collapse?

Yeah, I definitely do. I won't go anywhere near the coast trails now. And... well, I've kind of been dodging texts from my hiking buddies, too. Just because even talking about going out there, or thinking about it... it just makes my chest tighten up. So I just try to stay away from all of it.
Since the bluff collapse, have you been feeling numb or cut off from other people?

No, not really. I mean... I know I said I've been dodging my hiking buddies, but that's just because I don't want to talk about the trails. With everyone else... I don't feel numb or cut off. I still hang out with my roommates, and, you know, I talk to people on the phones at work all day. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel like that.
Since the bluff collapse, have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled?

No, not really. I don't think I'm any more jumpy than usual. I mean, I'm not sitting around feeling on edge or looking over my shoulder all the time or anything. So, no, I haven't really noticed feeling like that.
Since the bluff collapse, have you been blaming yourself for what happened?

Yeah, I do. I just... I keep thinking I was really stupid and careless for being out there alone in the first place. Like I should have known better. And because of that, it just feels like... if I let my guard down anywhere, something bad is going to happen.
Since the bluff collapse, have you often felt like the world is dangerous or that something bad could happen at any time?

Um... no, not really. I know I just said that thing about letting my guard down, but I mostly just meant about making sure I don't do something stupid again. I don't actually walk around thinking the whole world is super dangerous or... you know, that random bad things are just going to happen to me out of nowhere. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel like that.
Since the bluff collapse, have these symptoms been causing problems in your daily life or work?

Yeah, they have. It's definitely affecting my job. I work in customer service, and my focus has just been... off. I actually missed some important notes in the CRM system recently, which led to a call getting escalated. My manager wrote me up for it. I was really hoping to move up toward team lead soon, but now I'm worried I just completely blew my chance. 

And outside of work, it's been tough too. I'm supposed to be studying for my GED, but I've fallen pretty far behind. I'm just so exhausted all the time. Plus, I've been avoiding the friends I used to go hiking with, so I'm just kind of isolated right now.
Outside of thoughts or reminders of the bluff collapse, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, like my job and the GED stuff I mentioned, but it's not like I'm constantly stressing out about everything in my life. It's mostly just the stuff tied to the accident and how tired I am that's bothering me.
Since the bluff collapse, have you been feeling a lot of fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame?

Yeah. Um, mostly I'd say I feel scared and just... embarrassed. It's kind of always there under the surface most days. I feel like everyone can tell that I messed up out there. And... I don't know, it just makes me feel like I'm not as tough as I used to act before all this happened.
Since the bluff collapse, have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still like the same things. Like I said earlier, I haven't been hiking, but that's more about just... avoiding it, you know? Not because I don't like being outside anymore. I still enjoy playing video games and watching movies and stuff. I just haven't been doing as much in general lately because I'm always so tired. But the interest is still there.
Since the bluff collapse, have you often felt like you’re weak, worthless, or permanently damaged because of what happened?

Yeah, I do. Um... I just keep thinking about how stupid and careless I was for being out there alone in the first place. It makes me feel pretty dumb. And now... I don't know, it just feels like if I let my guard down anywhere, something bad is going to happen.
When those memories hit during the day, does it ever feel like the bluff collapse is happening again right then?

Yeah, it does. Stuff just... pops in my head out of nowhere. Like, I'll suddenly hear the sound of rocks sliding, or I'll feel like my leg is stuck under me again. And for a minute, it's like I'm right back on that trail, instead of just sitting at my desk with my headset on at work. It's really disorienting.
